reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Orient Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – No Report: Orient has good numbers of 9- to 10-inch fish.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Pleasant Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Fair: Look for suspended fish in deeper water or over deeper brush. Bluegill – Fair: Try fishing shallower water. Lots of smaller fish with bigger fish mixed in.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Red Rock Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: White Crappie – Fair: Catch crappies through September and October slowly trolling or drifting panfish plastics in arms off the main lake. Some of these include the South Overlook arm, Campetine Creek arm, and the Teter Creek arm.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Rice Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Fair: Use jigs or spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Silver Lake (Worth) fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Good: Cast jigs and spinnerbaits along vegetation.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Spirit Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Fair: Many nice-sized fish have been seen lately. Use minnows and plastics.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Turkey River (above Clermont) fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth Bass - Good: Find smallies in deeper holes or near rock ledges. Use a small jig or crankbait.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Twelve Mile Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Fair: Try jigs tipped with a minnow fished along creek channels in the flooded timber to catch black crappie up to 10 inches.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Upper Iowa River (above Decorah) fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth Bass - Good: Find fish near drop-offs, eddies, and rock ledges with a spinner or crankbait.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Volga Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Use tube jigs tipped with crappie nibbles off jetties. Also try trolling around the lake to find suspended fish.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Try fishing drop-offs and around brush piles and other attracting structures. Use crankbaits toward evening. Water levels on area rivers and streams remain low due to continuing drought conditions. Temperatures in the mid-70s to 50s though the weekend with a slight chance of rain. For current fishing information, please call the Chuck Gipp Decorah Fish Hatchery at 563-382-8324.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Wapsipinicon River (Troy Mills to Oxford Junction) fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth Bass – Fair.
reports.lake: Wapsipinicon River (Troy Mills to Oxford Junction)

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Beeds Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Good: Drift or slow troll small jigs to target suspended crappie.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Big Hollow Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: The cooler nights should bring cooler water temperatures that should get the crappies feeding more actively. Expect them to stay out in 6-7 feet of water for a while yet.
Largemouth Bass – Slow: Look for bass down at about 6 feet, no deeper. Flip soft plastics and jigs back into the flooded timber at 4-6 feet down to find them.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Brinker Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Reports of anglers catching crappie and largemouth bass.
Black Crappie – Slow: Use a slip bobber sinker and hook tipped with a minnow in brush piles in 6-8 feet of water.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Try plastics, spinnerbaits, or crankbaits in the afternoon to later evening.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Casey Lake (aka Hickory Hills Lake) fishing report
reports.text:
Anglers are having success with bluegill, black crappie, largemouth bass, and channel catfish.
Black Crappie – Good: Find structure using electronics and jig colored tube jigs at various depths to locate fish; the south corner of the damn has been really good for crappie.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Anglers are catching bass on most everything thrown at them; try spinners and crankbaits.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Cedar River (above Nashua) fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Find crappie in brush piles or around woody structure. Use a minnow under a bobber.
Smallmouth Bass - No report: Use a jig with a natural colored twister tail or nightcrawler in brush piles.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Cedar River (Nashua to La Porte City) fishing report
reports.text:
Target walleye, smallmouth bass, and channel catfish on the river in areas of deeper water with the low river conditions.
Smallmouth Bass – No Report: Try a jig with a twister and half of a crawler or cast crankbaits.
reports.lake: Cedar River (Nashua to La Porte City)

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Clear Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Fair: Anglers are catching a few crappie using live bait and small jigs.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Green Valley Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Slow: Catch largemouth bass up to 20-inches with finesse plastics fished along cedar tree brush piles.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Belva Deer fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Slow: Bass got pushed back a little with the return of the really hot weather. Forecast cooler weather should start to bring them in shallow again.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Hendricks fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie - Slow: Use a spinner or crankbait pulled slowly behind a small watercraft. Crappie are suspended throughout lake.
Largemouth Bass – Slow: Try a topwater or weedless lure along weed edges.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Meyer fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Slow: Crappies are suspended. Try trolling around the lake with a spinner or jig tipped with a light colored plastic tail.
Largemouth Bass – Slow: Try a topwater lure along the weed edges.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Little River Watershed Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Slow: Try finesse plastics fished along cedar tree brush piles or along rocky shoreline areas to catch all sizes of largemouth bass.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lost Grove Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Slow: Crappies are out along the edge of the flooded timber in 10 to 12 feet of water. Try vertical jigging or slow trolling until you find them. They are not in any rush to move shallower.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Most anglers are staying out in 10 to 12 feet of water; with the forecast cooler nights, expect to see bass start to work the shallower water more as the water temperature drops.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Maquoketa River (above Monticello) fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth Bass – No Report: Use a jig with a twister and half of a crawler or cast crankbaits.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 10 fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Use artificial jigs or a crappie minnow along the fallen trees in running sloughs in 6-8 feet of water.
Largemouth Bass – Good: Try fishing the edge of weed beds in backwater and side channel areas.
Smallmouth Bass – Good: Cast a spinner or crankbaits in current along the rocky shorelines.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 11 fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Use artificial jigs or a crappie minnow along the fallen trees in running sloughs in 6-8 feet of water.
Largemouth Bass – Good: Try fishing the edge of weed beds in backwater and side channel areas.
Smallmouth Bass – Good: Cast a spinner or crankbaits in current along the rocky shorelines.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 12 fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth Bass - Good: As we move into the fall months, largemouth bass fishing will improve as they start feeding heavily on bass.
Smallmouth Bass – Excellent: Cast inline spinners or crankbaits just off rock points to catch smallmouth feeding in the rocks. Lots of smallmouth have moved on to the wing-dams.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 13 fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Good: Some nice crappies are being caught out of the sluggish deeper side channels. Usually anglers are targeting wood piles in the river using small minnows.
Largemouth Bass – Excellent: Try plastics along vegetation lines.
Smallmouth Bass – Excellent: Cast inline spinners just off rock points to catch smallmouth feeding on minnows. Many smallmouth are also on the wing-dams, especially in this low water.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 14 fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie - Starting to hear anglers targeting crappies in side channels near fallen trees.
Largemouth Bass – Excellent: Try soft plastics along vegetation lines and brush piles.
Smallmouth Bass – Good: Cast inline spinners just off rock points to catch smallmouth feeding in the rocks; exposed wing-dam rock can be very good.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 16 fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – No Report: Look for largemouth bass around snags along main channel and side channels with the low water conditions.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 17 fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – No Report: Look for largemouth bass around brush piles and snags along the main channel and side channels with the low water conditions.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 18 fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – No Report: Look around brush piles and snags along main channel and side channels with low water conditions.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 9 fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Use artificial jigs or a crappie minnow along the fallen trees in rough sloughs in 6-8 feet of water.
Largemouth Bass – Good: Try fishing the edge of weed beds in backwater and side channel areas.
Smallmouth Bass – Good: Cast a spinner or crankbaits in current along the rocky shorelines.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Prairie Rose Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Slow: Anglers report catching black crappie around the tree piles; fish average 10-inches.
Largemouth Bass – Fair.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Rice Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Good: Use surface lures or weedless jigs.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Twelve Mile Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Slow: Try jigs fished along rock piles to catch all sizes of largemouth bass.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Upper Iowa River (below Decorah) fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth Bass – Slow: Use a jig tipped with a crawler or crawdad in the deeper pools or around rock ledges. A bright colored crankbait also works.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Volga Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie - Slow: Slowly troll or paddle deeper water; use a spinner bait.
Largemouth Bass – Slow: Find bass around fish attracting structures. Area interior rivers and streams are low. Clarity is good on most area rivers and streams. Expect more seasonal weekend temperatures with daytime highs in the low 80s to upper 40’s overnight; no rain expected. For current fishing information, please call the Chuck Gipp Decorah Fish Hatchery at 563-382-8324.

reports.text:
Bass topwater bite has been good.
